role: The invariant BEAE connecting core -- the FROZEN scaffold for the Fig-6 / L5 linker-frozen optimization, and the canonical head/tail decomposition for BEAE lipids.
concept: A BEAE lipid = (variable head) + (variable tail1) + (variable tail2) fused by a FIXED 12-atom linker (11 frozen core atoms + the shared central N's 3 attachment carbons). The head/tails vary; the linker does not.

atom_map_legend.1: central branch-point N (weakly-basic enamine junction; LINKER, not head)
atom_map_legend.4-5-6: acrylate-arm C(=O)-O ester (carbonyl C, =O, ester O)
atom_map_legend.12: tail1 attachment carbon (first atom of tail1; NOT frozen)
atom_map_legend.13: tail2 attachment carbon (first atom of tail2; NOT frozen)
atom_map_legend.14: head attachment carbon (first atom of the head spacer; NOT frozen)

invariant: 11 frozen linker-core atoms in every BEAE lipid, independent of head/tail identity (verified on RM-60, Example-2, H1-H4 heads).

generator_usage.fig6_linker_frozen: beae_linker_atoms(lead) -> the protected atom set; enforce as a HARD legal-fiber condition (remove any rewrite touching a frozen atom) so the linker survives by construction while the generator optimizes head + tail1 + tail2. Start from a measured lead via FixedMolecularStatePrior.
generator_usage.decomposition: beae_decompose(mol) -> {linker, head, tail1, tail2} atom sets (partition covers all heavy atoms).

region_labeling_relationship: This is the HARD version of the head/linker/tail split; lipid_region_labels is the SOFT per-atom version used for the region embedding + region-conditioned prior. Both put the central enamine N in the linker and the ionizable amine in the head.

provenance.scaffold_source: user figures (BEAE template + RM-60 + Example-2 + H1-H4)
